rule: Choose evidence by mechanism and claim (#4013, replacing #2761's universal Zen 5 requirement for eligible claims). A Zen 5 or microarchitecture-sensitive claim (SIMD width or intrinsics, branched versus branchless selection, instruction scheduling, latency or ports, store forwarding, alignment, prefetch, cache or TLB tuning, or an explicit Zen 5 speed claim) requires actual execution of its relevant workload on the approved Zen 5 benchmark host (AMD Ryzen 7 9700X); simulated, static and non-target evidence never satisfies it. A work-reduction or scaling claim may complete with work-count evidence, and an end-to-end native runtime or resource claim that does not depend on a particular CPU mechanism may complete with paired uninstrumented native-host evidence, each only for what that class establishes. Without complete evidence of the required class matching the candidate, workload and configuration, that claim's validation is incomplete. A non-Zen-5 class never records zen5: covered.

zen5-native.establishes: the claimed behavior on the approved physical Ryzen 7 9700X for the measured workload and configuration

work-count.establishes: less executed work (instructions, references, operations) for the measured workload and inputs, from repeatable instrumented or counted runs of both arms in one environment
work-count.does_not_establish: lower elapsed time; hardware-independent constants; Zen 5 behavior

native-host.establishes: an uninstrumented paired wall, CPU or resource change for the stated workload on the observed host and OS
native-host.does_not_establish: transfer to Zen 5 or to another CPU, OS, filesystem or concurrency level
